senses.en: a machine, tool or idea that somebody has made for the first time
examples: The light bulb was one of the most useful **inventions** of the 19th century.
My little brother showed us his own **invention**: a robot made of paper cups.
Which **invention** has changed your daily life the most?

senses.en: the act of making something that did not exist before
senses.vi: việc sáng chế, sự phát minh
examples: The **invention** of the smartphone changed how we talk to each other.
Life became much faster after the **invention** of the aeroplane.

forms.en: a person who makes something new
forms.ex: Thomas Edison was a famous American **inventor**.

forms.en: good at thinking of new ideas
forms.vi: sáng tạo, giàu óc sáng chế
forms.ex: She is very **inventive** and always finds a clever solution.

invention.note: Use *the* **invention of** + noun when you mean the moment something was first made: *the invention of the printing press*.

senses.en: to make or design something completely new for the first time
examples: Who **invented** the telephone?
Students at our school **invented** a bag that charges a phone using sunlight.
Engineers are trying to **invent** a cheaper way to clean sea water.

forms.en: something new that has been made
forms.ex: The wheel is a very old **invention**.
The **inventor** received a prize for her design.

invent.note: **Invent** = create something that never existed (*Bell invented the telephone*). *Discover* = find something that was already there (*Scientists discovered a new planet*). This is a very common learner mistake.

senses.en: the use of body features such as fingerprints, faces or eyes to check who a person is
examples: **Biometrics** is now used at most international airports.
Our new phone uses **biometrics** instead of a password.
**Biometrics** makes it harder for someone to steal your identity.

forms.en: connected with measuring features of the human body
forms.ex: The school gate has a **biometric** scanner.

biometrics.note: **Biometrics** ends in *-s* but takes a **singular** verb: *Biometrics **is** used in banks.* (like *physics*, *economics*). Before a noun, use the adjective **biometric**: *a biometric passport*.

senses.en: the mark made by the lines on the end of your finger, which is different for every person
examples: I unlock my laptop with my **fingerprint**.
The police found a **fingerprint** on the glass.
No two people in the world have the same **fingerprints**.

fingerprint.note: Written as one word. The machine that reads it is a **fingerprint scanner** or **fingerprint reader**.

senses.en: the coloured ring around the black centre of your eye
examples: The camera scans your **iris** before the door opens.
Her **irises** are a very dark brown.
**Iris** recognition is faster than typing a password.

senses.en: a tall garden flower with long thin leaves, usually purple, blue or yellow
examples: My grandmother grows purple **irises** beside the pond.
There were yellow **irises** all along the river.

iris.note: Plural: **irises**. In technology texts you will almost always meet the eye meaning, as in *iris scanning*.

senses.en: the act of knowing who or what somebody or something is, especially by a machine
senses.vi: sự nhận dạng, sự nhận diện
examples: Face **recognition** lets you pay without a card.
Voice **recognition** software can type what you say.
**Recognition** of your fingerprint takes less than a second.

senses.en: public praise for what somebody has done well
senses.vi: sự công nhận, sự ghi nhận
examples: The young scientist finally got the **recognition** she deserved.
He received a medal in **recognition** of his work on clean energy.

forms.en: to know somebody or something because you have seen it before
forms.ex: The app **recognises** my face even in the dark.

recognition.note: British spelling **recognise**; American spelling *recognize*. Both are pronounced the same.

senses.en: a piece of equipment made to do a particular job
examples: This small **device** measures the air quality in the room.
You can log in on up to three **devices**.
Please switch off all electronic **devices** during the test.

device.note: **Device** is countable: *a device*, *two devices*. Use *equipment* (uncountable) for the general idea: *lab equipment*, not ~~lab equipments~~.

senses.en: the ability of computers to do things that normally need human thinking, such as learning and making decisions
examples: **Artificial intelligence** can translate a whole book in seconds.
Doctors use **artificial intelligence** to read X-ray pictures.
Our teacher explained how **artificial intelligence** learns from data.

artificial intelligence.note: Uncountable — no *a/an* and no plural. It is usually shortened to **AI**: *an AI tool*, *AI is changing schools*. Say the two letters: /ˌeɪ ˈaɪ/.

senses.en: to make a machine or computer do a job that people used to do
examples: The factory has **automated** most of its packing work.
We can **automate** the watering of the school garden.
Many boring office tasks are now **automated**.

forms.en: the use of machines to do work instead of people
forms.ex: **Automation** has changed the way cars are built.

forms.en: working by itself without a person controlling it
forms.ex: The lights in the corridor are **automatic**.

automate.note: **Automatic** describes a thing; **automatically** describes how something happens: *The door opens **automatically***.

senses.en: a way of studying in which you learn a very small amount at a time, usually in lessons of a few minutes
senses.vi: học siêu ngắn (học theo từng đoạn rất ngắn)
examples: **Nanolearning** is popular with students who are always busy.
With **nanolearning**, five minutes on the bus is enough for one lesson.
Our app uses **nanolearning** to teach ten new words a week.

nanolearning.note: A very new word, so many dictionaries do not have it yet. *Nano-* means *extremely small*, so **nanolearning** means learning in very short bursts — often two to five minutes on a phone. Compare *microlearning*, which means almost the same thing.

senses.en: doing a job well without wasting time, money or energy
examples: Electric trains are more **efficient** than old diesel ones.
This robot is **efficient**: it does in one hour what took us a day.
We need a more **efficient** way to sort the rubbish.

forms.en: the quality of working well without waste
forms.ex: The new engine improved the car's **efficiency**.

forms.en: in a way that does not waste time or energy

efficient.note: **Efficient** = no waste of time or energy. *Effective* = it gives the result you want. A method can be *effective* but not **efficient** if it takes too long.

senses.en: using new ideas or new ways of doing things
examples: The team won the prize for their **innovative** water filter.
Our school has a very **innovative** way of teaching science.
Viet Nam has many **innovative** young start-ups.

forms.en: a new idea or method, or the making of new ideas
forms.ex: This app is the biggest **innovation** in online learning this year.

forms.en: to introduce new ideas or methods
forms.ex: Companies must **innovate** or they will lose customers.

senses.en: an important discovery or change that helps you make progress after a long time
examples: Scientists have made a **breakthrough** in the treatment of malaria.
The new battery is a real **breakthrough** for electric cars.
After months of failure, they finally had a **breakthrough**.

breakthrough.note: The noun is one word, **breakthrough**; the verb phrase is two words: *break through*. We usually say **make** a breakthrough, not ~~do~~ a breakthrough.

senses.en: a room or building where scientists do tests and research
examples: The samples were sent to a **laboratory** for testing.
You must wear glasses and gloves in the **laboratory**.
Our school built a new computer **laboratory** last year.

laboratory.note: The short, everyday form is **lab**: *the school lab*, *lab coat*. Stress differs: British *la-**BOR**-a-try*, American ***LAB**-ra-tory*.

senses.en: a scientific test done to find out what happens or to prove an idea
examples: We did an **experiment** with salt and ice in class today.
The **experiment** showed that the plants grew faster in blue light.
Her first **experiment** failed, so she tried again.

senses.en: to try new things or do scientific tests to see what happens
examples: The class **experimented** with different kinds of soil.
Scientists are **experimenting** with a new kind of plastic.
I like to **experiment** with recipes at the weekend.

forms.en: connected with tests, or still being tested
forms.ex: The hospital is using an **experimental** drug.

experiment.note: The noun and the verb are spelt the same but stressed differently in careful speech, and we say **do** or **carry out** an experiment — not ~~make an experiment~~.

senses.en: to take the place of somebody or something else
examples: Will robots **replace** teachers in the future?
Email has largely **replaced** letters.
Nothing can **replace** a good night's sleep.

senses.en: to put a new or different thing in the position of an old one
examples: We had to **replace** the broken screen.
The school **replaced** all the old lights with LED ones.

senses.en: to put something back where it was before
examples: Please **replace** the books on the shelf when you finish.
He **replaced** the lid carefully so nothing spilled.

replace.note: Say **replace** A **with** B (*We replaced the old PC with a laptop*), or *A was replaced **by** B*. Do not say ~~replace A by a new one~~ in the active voice.

senses.en: a good effect or advantage that something brings
examples: One **benefit** of online learning is that you can study anywhere.
The **benefits** of exercise are well known.
New technology brings both **benefits** and problems.

senses.en: to be helped by something, or to help somebody
senses.vi: hưởng lợi; mang lại lợi ích cho
examples: Farmers **benefit** from weather apps on their phones.
The whole village **benefited** from the new solar panels.
Clean water **benefits** everyone.

forms.ex: Reading before bed is **beneficial** for sleep.

benefit.note: The opposite is **drawback** or *disadvantage*. Note the spelling of the verb forms: **benefited**, **benefiting** (one *t* in British and American English).

senses.en: a bad point or problem that makes something less good
examples: The main **drawback** of the robot is its high price.
Studying online has one big **drawback**: you miss your friends.
Every new invention has some **drawbacks**.

drawback.note: **Drawback** is the opposite of **benefit** / *advantage*. It is countable, and it is often used in the pattern *The (main) drawback of X is that…*
